question: Türkiye prohibits the manufacture of cars with built-in navigation maps unless they are approved by the Turkish army. Car makers conforming to Turkish legislation therefore import cars into the EU without maps and add them at a later stage, either at European hubs or when they reach the national importers.

The result of this Turkish legislation and practice is a rise in cost and the additional burden this brings for European consumers. In other words, Türkiye is imposing its own foreign policy on factories, in contempt of the EU, which, be it noted, puts up with this and panders to Türkiye, forcing the European consumer to buy more expensive products. In view of the above: 1.
What measures does the Commission intend to take to protect European consumers from the increased financial burden due to Turkish legislation?
Does it intend to take measures to counter Turkish policy which affects the manufacture of products for the EU single market?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.3.2025) Türkiye has since 1996 a Customs Union with the EU, but it is not part of the European single market. The car manufacturers that have chosen to produce cars in Türkiye and export them to the EU have to introduce navigation maps that comply with the EU ‘whole vehicle type’ approval (Regulation (EU)2021/19581).

Turkish map data approval is only needed for products (imported or produced locally) that will enter and be registered in the Turkish market. In other words, EU map data, even if it contradicts Türkiye’s Map Law, can be imported to be used in mass production in Türkiye and then be exported again.

Therefore, the fact that the car manufacturers in Türkiye need to use two separate navigation systems for the domestic and export markets does not seem to have a cost effect on the cars sold in the EU.

Should the EU industry consider this issue a trade barrier they should provide all the relevant information to the Commission and there is a single entry point procedure for market access complaints at the Commission they can use for this purpose.
